not_claimed: No requirement is Verified; G6 qualification (OCOR-DEV-0060..0066) is not anticipated.
NFR-065 RTO/RPO is NOT demonstrated: the drill measures restore duration on synthetic fixtures; the target is defined from declared fault to mission-thread validation, which is G6 work.

Restore steps rebuild_logic_projection_and_w3c_boundary and run_conformance_security_mission_thread_replay are recorded NOT_EXECUTED in every receipt; reopening the mutative path requires human authorization.

Authority classes action and model_scenario have no store deployed at G4 and are recorded as NO_STORE_DEPLOYED_AT_G4 in each manifest; key custody is OpenBao transit in bootstrap dev mode (in-memory, not durable across OpenBao restarts).
Single custodian for transit keys in the PoC stack: dual control of key access is not exercised.
Trace fields not produced by the ops plane (GovernedContext of C1-C8 boundaries) are emitted as null and listed as unavailable, never fabricated.
action_adapter_timeout and edge_partition faults are not observable by the ops plane at G4 and are reported as such in /posture.

The Compose carrier has no scheduler: the 15-minute backup cadence is enforced by the Helm CronJob; with Compose it requires a host scheduler, and RPO compliance is exported as ocor_recovery_point_within_rpo.

residual_risks: Memory backup/restore is exercised on a synthetic drill binding (ocor_poc_drill database and Qdrant collection) until the G5 memory stores exist (DEC-208 fence).

The Compose default-deny is realized by an internal network plus one relay per allowed flow (own address, own port); the kind NetworkPolicy enforcement depends on the kindnet implementation of the disposable cluster.
The stuck-scanner branch (SCAN_STALE) is proven at decision-logic level only: it cannot be provoked on the real process without also stopping its HTTP server.
The governed reopening authenticates the operator with the bootstrap operator token and records a named human; it is not bound to a Keycloak identity or dual control in the PoC ops plane.
Fault injection uses docker pause (not stop) to avoid destroying tmpfs-backed bootstrap state and the SPIRE agent attestation.

kindnet programs the NetworkPolicy of a newly created pod asynchronously: in that window the agent itself observes and reports PUBLIC_EGRESS_OPEN and the pod stays NotReady (fail-closed); the Helm test waits for convergence before asserting that the release fence is the only remaining reason.

The release fence binds a tested restore to the FULL profile digest: any profile change, including operational tuning, requires a new backup and recovery-gate pass before readiness (most restrictive fail-closed reading, recorded).

The ops agent does not inspect its own image id from inside the pod: executed image == governed pin holds by construction (single source pin -> rendered image, refused overrides) and is observed on Compose (container image id) and kind (pod imageID).
The policy inventory bound is 4 MiB: a legitimate inventory above it is reported POLICY_INVENTORY_TOO_LARGE (no digest in telemetry) rather than truncated.
La deriva dell’ID locale Fuseki non è risolta: base/source della ricetta CI pinned, ID reale acquisito per ogni run, nessuna uguaglianza col lock asserita.
